column2: Your INMP441 seen from the pin side: SCK, WS, L/R in one row, SD, VDD, GND in the other. SCK faces SD, WS faces VDD, L/R faces GND.

Plug the INMP441 across the center gap in columns 26 to 28, like an IC: the spacing between its two pin rows equals the spacing from row e to row f. The sound hole faces up. The SCK, WS, L/R row goes in row f, the SD, VDD, GND row in row e: f26 SCK, f27 WS, f28 L/R, e26 SD, e27 VDD, e28 GND. Do not plug both pin rows on the same side (for example a and d): the five holes of a column are connected, so SCK would be shorted to SD.

Wires for pins in row f come from row j, wires for pins in row e from row a, in the same column. Check the labels on your module first; if the order differs, keep this rule and the wire destinations stay the same.
Power (M-M wires): a27 (VDD) → red line (3.3 V; the INMP441 must not get 5 V), a28 (GND) → blue line, j28 (L/R) → b28 (the GND column, across the gap), so L/R also goes to GND.
Signals (F-M wires from the S pins of the expansion board): IO15 → j26 (SCK), IO16 → j27 (WS), IO6 → a26 (SD).
Always 0: SD and WS swapped, or the j28 → b28 wire (L/R to GND) is loose. Upload tes_mic_diagnosis to see which channel is alive.
INMP441 (f26-f28 SCK, WS, L/R; e26-e28 SD, VDD, GND)
